For 1<t<2, with no tight internal edges, connectedness gives integer-valued binary potentials. In ≥3 parts, disconnected nonconstant binary cuts occur exactly when a single mixed part has all other parts monochromatic: exclude 2∑(2^m_i−2) orientations. With a tight internal edge in part i, all outside vertices lie in [t−1,1], a band narrower than 1, so no outside tight edge; connectedness forces the unique saturated part's values {0,t} and every external value t−1 or1. This gives (2^m_i−2)2^(N−m_i) for each unique i; summing yields 2^N−2+∑(2^m_i−2)(2^(N−m_i)−2). Endpoint t=1 equilateral and t=2 previously known 2^N−2−∑(2^m_i−2), also follows directly. Singleton-only profile remains equilateral.
